newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end mixed on moderate volumes.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mixed Thursday, on moderate volumes, with gold finding some support, after weakness earlier in the month, and platinum group metals (PGMs) still firm while waiting for the return of Russian supplies.

"In gold the failure to get much more action on the downside prompted some fund shortcovering later in the session, after the expiry of the OTC options in London in the bullion market, but overall it was a quiet day," Refco New York analyst Tim Porter said.
COMEX August gold saw a new life-of-contract low early at $338.10 an ounce, before ending up 80 cents at $339.80. Estimated total COMEX gold volume was 36,000 lots.

Volume in COMEX gold has been lackluster in the past month averaging around 20,000 lots a day, but open interest has steadily climbed back to 185,491 contracts, the highest level since February, as gold prices have tested the four year lows seen earlier this year.

The momentum of the downtrend has increased a little in the past week, with a standard 14-day ADX indicator edging up to 20 percent, but 20-day historical volatility remains low around eight percent, analysts noted.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $338.00/50, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $336.95 an ounce, and the New York close Wednesday around $337.10/60, and not far from the four year low at $336.90 on February 12.

"There is every reason to believe the current price range of $340-350 per ounce will remain as a floor to the market, and that the market will be fairly stable under present economic circumstances," South Africa's Amgold (Anglo American Gold Investment Co Ltd) chairman, Nicky Oppenheimer said in his annual review statement Thursday.
COMEX September silver, now the active contract, ended down 1.5 cents at $4.790 an ounce, but has traded in a $4.70-4.90 range for six weeks now.
The spot gold/silver ratio ended around 71:1, after drifting down from a recent high at 73.5 in early April.
Meanwhile, the long wait for the return of Russian supplies to the market continued in the PGM complex.
The acute shortage of metal meant a rollover was negotiated on a large OTC market platinum call option at the $400 strike price which was due to expire Thursday, sources said.
The Swiss parties which wrote the option were not able to deliver the metal to the U.S. house holding the call, sources said.
In the physical market, the shortage of metal is keeping one month platinum lease rates around 60 pct, while one month palladium was seen around 90 pct, refining sources said.
NYMEX July platinum ended up $1.50 at $413.00 an ounce, while NYMEX September palladium closed up 25 cents at $181.40 an ounce.
But open interest in both NYMEX platinum and palladium has declined sharply in the past month on speculative long liquidation ahead of the resumption of Russian exports, analysts said.

Spot platinum prices hit a seven year high earlier this month and spot palladium prices a 17 year high due to the six month suspension of Russian PGM exports. Russian supplies are expected to resume in late June or early July.
Russia supplies about 20 percent of the world's platinum and 60 pct of its palladium.
